title: Decision: Emit state event only when a row is actually affected
description:
Throughout message.rs and contact.rs, StateChange is emitted only when :
  - update_delivery_state: emit only if UPDATE touched 1+ rows (line 292)
  - update_read_at: emit only if UPDATE touched 1+ rows (line 362)
  - set_blocked: emit only if UPDATE touched 1+ rows (not shown, but test at line 603 verifies)

This is correct because:
1. RFC 8620 §7.1 state tokens represent actual changes, not spurious advances
2. If a query affects 0 rows (nonexistent ID or already-terminal state), the state should not advance
3. Test 'test_set_blocked_noop_no_emit' (line 603) explicitly verifies no-op calls don't emit
4. Test 'update_delivery_state_delivered_is_terminal' (line 782) verifies terminal state is idempotent
5. Prevents phantom state counters: every state token has a matching row with state_version

This is correct application of RFC 8620 semantics: state is data, not a logical clock that advances on every call.
